title: Leading a large migration (UIKit→SwiftUI, ObjC→Swift, monolith→modules)
summary: Big migrations succeed when they are incremental, measurable and safe to pause: define why, migrate in small slices behind clear rules, track progress on a dashboard, and make the new way the easy way.
body: **Why interviewers ask:** staff engineers are expected to lead multi-quarter changes across many teams. They want to hear how you reduce risk and bring people along, not just the technology.
**1. Start with the why and the metric:** "UIKit screens take 2× longer to build" or "build time is 12 minutes". Without a measurable goal the migration never finishes.
**2. Write a plan (RFC/ADR):** options considered, chosen approach, risks, rollout, how to measure success, what we are **not** doing. Get feedback from affected teams early.

**3. Strangler pattern:** new code in the new way; old code migrated when touched or by priority (most-changed screens first). Both worlds coexist through bridges (`UIHostingController`, bridging headers, interface modules).
**4. Make it easy:** templates, code generators, lint rules that block new old-style code, a migration guide with examples from your codebase, office hours, pairing.
**5. De-risk:** feature flags per migrated screen, A/B comparison of performance and crash rate, phased rollout.
**6. Track and communicate:** dashboard (% screens migrated, % Swift, build time), regular updates to leadership, celebrate milestones.
**7. Finish:** plan the long tail (the last 10% is the hardest); delete the old path, otherwise you maintain two systems forever.
**Answer structure (STAR):** Situation, Task, Action (the steps above), Result (numbers!), and what you would do differently.
keyPoints: Clear why + measurable goal before starting.
RFC/ADR with options, risks and non-goals; involve affected teams early.
Incremental strangler approach with bridges between old and new.
Lint rules + templates make the new way the default.
Flags and phased rollout; dashboard; plan and finish the long tail.
mistakes: A "big bang" rewrite that freezes feature work.
Starting without metrics, so success cannot be shown.
Leaving the migration at 80% and maintaining both worlds.
followups: **How did you convince leadership?** Cost of not migrating in engineer-hours and incidents, plus a plan that keeps shipping features.
**How do you handle a team that refuses to migrate?** Understand their constraints, offer help/pairing, adjust timeline, escalate only with data.
**What would you migrate first?** High-change, low-risk areas that prove the approach and build confidence.
